passage: After-school club note, Wednesday. Preeti came in furious. Her mother had taken her tablet at bedtime the night before, after two warnings, and Preeti said it was cheating because she was in the middle of a level. She slammed her pencil case shut. Later she said quietly, "I miss it." I told her that losing something fun hurts, and she admitted she had once hidden the tablet under her blanket. I asked what might work better than hiding it. She thought and said, "If we knew the time in advance, it wouldn't be a surprise." I suggested she ask her mother for a fixed schedule. On Friday she told me they had agreed one, and she looked lighter. — Mr Vijay, club supervisor

qa.q: Who took Preeti's tablet, and when?
qa.a: Her mother took it at bedtime the night before.

qa.q: What is Preeti really upset about underneath her fury, and what hints at it?
qa.a: She was upset at losing something fun; her quiet "I miss it" shows the hurt under the anger.

qa.q: Why is agreeing a fixed schedule a better choice for Preeti than hiding the tablet?
qa.a: With a known time there is no surprise to fight about and no need to sneak, and her mother can trust her more. 🙂

qa.q: How might Preeti's mother have seen that bedtime moment?
qa.a: As the end of a limit she had already warned about twice, when it was time to stop for the night.

grounding: A child furious at a parent taking her tablet admits she misses it and negotiates a fixed schedule.

passage:
In the swimming club's waiting lounge, Nandini was three levels deep in her puzzle game when the coach called her group. She didn't hear. Her friend Hafsa was already in the pool.
Mumma walked over, took the tablet and slid it into her bag. "You've missed the warm-up. Go."
"That's not fair! I was about to finish!" Nandini's cheeks burned. She stomped to the changing room and yanked her cap on so hard it pulled her hair.
In the water, the anger slowly dripped away. It wasn't really about fairness. She had just been having fun, and it vanished in one second.
On the drive home she said, "Can we make a plan? Tablet after swimming, not before. And you give me a five-minute warning?"
Mumma raised an eyebrow, then smiled. "Deal. That's better than me grabbing it."

qa.q: What did Nandini miss because she was playing?
What was Nandini really feeling underneath her anger?
qa.a: On top she felt cheated and furious, but underneath she was upset at losing her fun so suddenly.

qa.q: What plan did Nandini suggest, and why is it better than sneaking the tablet?
qa.a: Tablet after swimming, with a five-minute warning; it is agreed openly, so nobody grabs or hides anything.

qa.q: How might Mumma have seen the moment she took the tablet?
qa.a: She was probably frustrated that Nandini had missed the warm-up and acted quickly to get her into the pool.

grounding: A girl is furious when her mother takes the tablet, realises she is upset at losing her fun, and proposes an agreed schedule.

passage:
Thursday: At nine sharp, Papa unplugged the tablet in the middle of a game. "Bedtime." Jagdish threw his pillow. "You're so mean! You always ruin everything!" He lay awake fuming, feeling robbed.
Saturday: At Tanvir's flat, Tanvir whispered, "Play on my phone. Your papa won't know." They hid behind the sofa. But every time a door opened, Jagdish jumped. The game wasn't even fun. He handed the phone back after ten minutes.
Monday: After dinner Jagdish sat beside Papa with a notebook. "What if I get one hour after homework, two on Sundays, and you don't pull the plug mid-level? I'll stop at the end of a level myself."
Papa read the page twice. "Let's try it for a week." They both signed it.

qa.q: At what time did Papa unplug the tablet?
How did Jagdish feel lying awake on Thursday night?
qa.a: Furious and robbed, as if Papa had ruined everything.

qa.q: Why did negotiating work better than sneaking for Jagdish?
qa.a: Sneaking at Tanvir's made him jumpy and wasn't even fun, while the written plan gave him screen time openly with Papa's agreement.

qa.q: How might Papa see Jagdish's notebook plan?
qa.a: He takes it seriously, reading it twice, and is willing to try because Jagdish came to him calmly.

grounding: A boy furious at his father for taking the tablet finds sneaking screens joyless and negotiates a fixed schedule instead.
